title: OOP, Modules, File I/O & Log Analysis
intro: Classes, modules, packages, files, CSV, JSON and practical log analysis.

sec.s: Python programs become easier to organize as they grow.

b.x: Python programs become easier to organize as they grow. A short script might calculate a total or print a message, but a larger application may need to represent users, products, orders, files, security events, and reports. Object-oriented programming (OOP), modules, packages, and file input/output help organize such programs.
Object-oriented programming organizes code around objects that combine data and behavior. A Student object might store a student’s name and marks and provide a method for calculating an average.
Modules let you place related Python code in separate files. A module can contain functions, classes, constants, and other statements. Packages organize related modules into directories.

File I/O means reading data from files and writing data to files. Text files are suitable for plain text, CSV files store tabular data, and JSON files represent structured data commonly exchanged by APIs.

Log analysis means examining records generated by a program, operating system, web server, or security tool. Logs can help identify failed logins, unusual activity, errors, and operational problems. A Python script can read log files, parse entries, count events, and produce a report.
These subjects connect naturally

x: A class can represent a security event.
A module can contain the parser that converts a log line into an event.
File I/O can load the log and save the report.
A package can organize all the components of a small monitoring tool.

b.x: Examples use Python 3. The exact format of real system logs depends on the operating system and the service that produced them.

sec.s: OOP is a programming approach built around objects.

b.x: OOP is a programming approach built around objects. An object has state and behavior. State is represented by data, often stored in attributes. Behavior is represented by methods, which are functions defined in a class.
For example, a bank-account object might store an account holder and balance. Its methods might deposit money, withdraw money, and display a balance.
Four commonly taught OOP principles are

x: Encapsulation: keep data and the operations that manage it together, and provide a clear interface.
Inheritance: create a class based on another class to reuse or specialize behavior.
Polymorphism: allow different object types to respond to the same operation in their own way.
Abstraction: expose essential behavior while hiding unnecessary implementation details.

b.x: These principles are tools, not rules requiring every program to use every feature. Python also supports procedural programming and functional programming. Use OOP when objects with related state and behavior make the design clearer.

sec.s: A class is a definition describing a type of object.

b.x: A class is a definition describing a type of object. An object is an instance created from that class.
class Student: defines a class. pass is a placeholder statement that does nothing. Student() creates an instance. The two objects are separate instances, even though they come from the same class.
A more useful class stores information
Here, name and course are instance attributes. Each student object can have different values.
Classes make it easier to represent many similar entities:
A class does not automatically store data permanently. Ordinary in-memory objects disappear when the program exits unless their data is saved to a file, database, or another persistent system.

sec.s: An attribute is a value associated with an object or class.

b.x: An attribute is a value associated with an object or class. A method is a function defined in a class.
width and height are instance attributes. area() and perimeter() are instance methods.

In an instance method, self refers to the particular object on which the method is called. It is the conventional parameter name; Python does not use a special keyword for it, but using self is standard practice.
When you write rectangle.area(), Python effectively supplies rectangle as the first argument to the method. You normally do not write rectangle.area(rectangle).
Each instance has its own attributes
Methods can validate data, update state, calculate values, and coordinate operations. A well-designed class keeps related behavior together.

b.x: Encapsulation means grouping data and behavior together and defining how callers should interact with an object’s state. It helps prevent invalid changes and hides internal implementation details behind a public interface.

Python naming conventions include: - name: public attribute. - _name: non-public implementation detail by convention. - __name: triggers name mangling in many class contexts, helping avoid accidental name collisions. It is not absolute security or true privacy.

sec.s: Inheritance lets a new class reuse and specialize an existing class.

b.x: Inheritance lets a new class reuse and specialize an existing class. The existing class is the base or parent class, and the derived class is the child or subclass.
Dog inherits the initializer and name attribute from Animal, while it overrides speak().
super() lets a subclass call behavior from the next class in the method resolution order:

Introductory textbooks commonly describe single, multilevel, hierarchical, multiple, and hybrid inheritance. Python supports multiple inheritance. When multiple bases define a method with the same name, Python uses the method resolution order (MRO) to determine where to look. ClassName.mro() displays that order.

Inheritance is suitable when a subclass genuinely represents a specialized kind of the base class and can be used wherever the base class is expected. Do not use inheritance solely to reuse a few lines of code. Composition may be clearer: a car has an engine; it is not an engine.

sec.s: Polymorphism means that the same operation can work with different object types, with each type providing…

b.x: Polymorphism means that the same operation can work with different object types, with each type providing its own behavior.

Both objects respond to speak(), even though they are instances of different classes. Python commonly uses duck typing: if an object supports the operations needed by code, the code can often use it regardless of its exact class.
Any object that supplies a compatible speak() method can work. If it does not, Python raises an attribute error. Type hints or protocols can document the expected interface.
Classes can also customize operators through special methods such as __add__():
Operator overloading should preserve reasonable expectations. Do not make an operator behave in a surprising way.

sec.s: Abstraction presents important behavior while leaving implementation details behind a clear interface.

b.x: Abstraction presents important behavior while leaving implementation details behind a clear interface. Python’s abc module supports abstract base classes.
An abstract class with an unimplemented abstract method cannot normally be instantiated until a concrete subclass provides the required implementation.
Composition builds a larger object by combining smaller objects:

Service has a Logger; it does not need to inherit from Logger. Composition can make software easier to extend because the contained component can be replaced with another object that offers the same interface.

sec.s: Pitfalls and fixes

b.x: Good OOP does not mean creating a class for every value. A small calculation may be better as a function. Use classes when a meaningful entity has state, behavior, or a clear interface.

Common mistakes: 1. Forgetting self in an instance method definition. 2. Calling an instance method without an instance. 3. Forgetting super().__init__() when inherited initialization is needed. 4. Changing attributes in ways that violate class rules. 5. Assuming a leading underscore makes an attribute secure or inaccessible. 6. Using inheritance only to reuse code. 7. Writing one enormous class that handles everything. 8. Giving methods unrelated responsibilities. 9. Confusing a class with an instance. 10. Assuming ordinary object data is persistent. 11. Assuming two variables referring to the same object are independent copies.
A class should have a clear purpose. Keep validation near the state it protects, give methods descriptive names, and test normal and boundary conditions.

sec.s: A module is a Python file that can define functions, classes, variables, and executable statements.

b.x: A module is a Python file that can define functions, classes, variables, and executable statements. A file named math_tools.py can be imported as a module named math_tools.

Modules separate concerns, enable code reuse, and make testing and maintenance easier. Python includes standard-library modules such as math, json, csv, pathlib, datetime, and collections. A custom module is simply a module you write yourself.

import math binds the module name, so use math.sqrt(). from pathlib import Path imports the name Path directly. Avoid from module import * in ordinary application code because it makes name origins unclear.

You can import specific names or use an alias:
The if __name__ == "__main__" pattern
A module’s __name__ is set to "__main__" when the file is run as the main program. When imported, it normally contains the module’s import name.

This lets a file be run directly while preventing its main routine from automatically running just because another module imports it. Top-level definitions still execute during import, so avoid unnecessary side effects at import time.

Common import problems include wrong directories, misspelled names, filenames shadowing standard modules (for example, naming your file json.py), circular imports, and running a file from an unexpected working directory. Use unique filenames and keep imports predictable.

sec.s: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a text format for structured data, common in APIs and configuration…

b.x: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a text format for structured data, common in APIs and configuration files. JSON supports objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. In Python, JSON objects usually become dictionaries, arrays become lists, and JSON true, false, and null become True, False, and None.
Write JSON
json.dump() writes to a file. indent=2 makes output readable, while ensure_ascii=False preserves non-ASCII characters in readable form.
Read JSON

Distinguish file operations from string operations: - json.dump(object, file) writes to a file. - json.dumps(object) returns a JSON-formatted string. - json.load(file) reads JSON from a file. - json.loads(text) parses a JSON string.

JSON does not directly represent every Python object, such as an arbitrary class instance, set, or file handle. Convert custom objects to supported structures, usually dictionaries and lists. Parsing verifies syntax, not business rules. Validate required keys, types, ranges, and permissions after loading.

sec.s: File operations can fail.

b.x: File operations can fail. Common exceptions include FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, IsADirectoryError, UnicodeDecodeError, csv.Error, json.JSONDecodeError, and the broader OSError.
Handle expected failures with focused exception handling:

Avoid a broad except Exception: that hides every failure unless you have a strong reason and log or re-raise the problem appropriately. Error handling should make failure understandable, not silently pretend the operation succeeded.

For important outputs, writing to a temporary file and then replacing the destination can reduce the chance of leaving a partially written file if a process fails. Robust designs may also require backups, permissions, checksums, and platform-specific considerations.

sec.s: A log is a record of an event produced by a system or application.

b.x: A log is a record of an event produced by a system or application. Examples include authentication successes and failures, server requests, application errors, file access, service startup/shutdown, and firewall events.
Log analysis can help identify failures and suspicious patterns. It is not a substitute for authentication, access control, endpoint protection, or dedicated security monitoring.
A fictional authentication log might contain
The IP addresses are documentation-only example ranges. Real logs vary in format. Some are plain text, some JSON, and others follow syslog or web-server conventions.

A practical workflow: 1. Locate the log source and confirm permission to read it. 2. Understand the format and its fields. 3. Parse records into structured data. 4. Validate fields and handle malformed records. 5. Filter relevant events, such as failed authentication or high-severity errors. 6. Aggregate results by user, address, event type, or time. 7. Interpret carefully: repeated failures may indicate an attack, but could also be caused by a misconfigured client or forgotten password. 8. Report and investigate; correlate with other evidence before drawing strong conclusions. 9. Protect the data because logs may contain personal information, session identifiers, internal addresses, or secrets.

Possible indicators include many failed logins in a short period, repeated failures against multiple accounts from one source, one account failing from many sources, unexpected privilege changes, and sudden increases in errors. No single indicator proves malicious behavior. Thresholds depend on the environment and should be tested to avoid excessive false positives.

sec.s: Log analysis is defensive when performed on systems and data you are authorized to inspect.

b.x: Log analysis is defensive when performed on systems and data you are authorized to inspect. Important precautions: - Read only logs you are authorized to access. - Do not publish raw logs containing usernames, email addresses, session tokens, access tokens, passwords, or personal data. - Never commit secrets to a repository. - Restrict permissions on reports and archives. - Retain logs only as long as policy and operational needs require. - Preserve timestamps and time zones when correlating events. - Record how reports were generated and which input files were used. - Do not treat an IP address as definitive proof of a person’s identity or intent. - Avoid automatic punitive action based only on a simple threshold. - Sanitize untrusted content before displaying it in terminals, dashboards, or reports. - Consider log injection: user-controlled newline characters or misleading strings can make a log appear to contain false records. Structured logging and proper escaping help reduce this risk.
Treat log content as data, not executable code. Never run commands constructed from log fields. Do not use eval() or execute parsed content. Parse expected formats and validate values.

sec.s: Testing checks that code behaves as expected.

b.x: Testing checks that code behaves as expected. A simple assertion verifies a result:
For a parser, test valid events, blank lines, missing event names, malformed fields, unexpected values, Unicode characters, empty files, and missing files.
This assumes parse_line() is available in the same module or imported correctly.

Debugging workflow: 1. Read the traceback and identify the line that failed. 2. Check file path, working directory, and permissions. 3. Inspect the type and structure of a parsed record. 4. Test the smallest failing input. 5. Distinguish syntax errors from valid-but-unexpected data. 6. Record the error category without leaking sensitive raw contents. 7. Add a regression test after fixing a bug.
A parser that works for one sample line may fail on real logs with spaces, missing fields, or different date formats. Test with representative, redacted examples.

sec.s: Recap and checklist

b.x: Summary

OOP uses classes to define object structure and behavior. Objects are instances of classes. Attributes represent state and methods represent behavior. __init__() initializes a newly created instance, while self refers to the current instance.

Encapsulation groups data and operations and encourages callers to use a controlled interface. Python uses naming conventions rather than strict access control for most ordinary attributes. Inheritance allows specialization and reuse; super() accesses the next implementation in the method resolution order. Polymorphism allows different objects to respond to the same operation. Abstraction defines essential interfaces, and composition combines objects without requiring inheritance.

A module is a Python file. Custom modules can be imported with import or from ... import .... The if __name__ == "__main__": pattern separates direct execution from import behavior. Packages organize modules into directories, while virtual environments isolate dependencies.

File I/O persists data. Use context managers to close files reliably. Text files store character data, CSV files represent tables through csv, and JSON files represent structured data through json. Parsing does not automatically validate correctness, so validate values and handle expected errors.

Log analysis parses event records, filters relevant events, counts patterns, and creates reports. Security alerts should be interpreted carefully, and logs must be protected because they can contain sensitive information.
